data.why: The repo ships a complete, self-contained dummy language pack (languages/dummy) with a prebuilt SQLite corpus (testlang.db), FST grammar, and lexicon, which the app loads by default with no setup needed.

goals: Browse and annotate a corpus of utterances, assigning gold morphological analyses to each token span
Run the finite-state morphological analyzer on a word or phrase and inspect the interpretations it proposes
Generate inflected word forms with the Phrase Builder by answering guided grammatical questions
Record a linguistic claim, link supporting or contradicting utterances as evidence, and track its status
Search the corpus by surface form, gloss, or grammatical tag to find examples of a pattern
Review dictionary entries (lexemes and morphology) generated from the language's FST grammar

review.summary: The tree describes the tool's core well: analyzer readings, gold annotation on the workbench, search and the dictionary, all with accurate labels and well-cut features. It falls short on claim tracking, which is one of the README's three purposes and never gets evidence linked. It also overstates two behaviours the screens contradict: span probing (043) and linking only the picked results (090).
